status_corrections.actual_source_outcome: The Definition assigns s_i^ell=1 exactly when the preactivation is strictly positive; hence an assigned active bit entails positivity. The nonpositive case, including zero, is explicitly assigned bit zero.

Conversely, a strictly positive preactivation is assigned bit one by the defining rule. Together with the explicit nonpositive/inactive convention, this exhausts all real preactivation values, including identically zero cells.

Zero hyperplanes m=0 are explicitly admitted. Proof step 1.1 gives R(0,d)=1, the entire ambient space as one region; the j=0 binomial term is one and all j>0 terms vanish. The separate zero-dimensional image likewise has one cell.

An individual folding block has width n>=3. For an empty composition of blocks, the layer-product convention gives one and the unprocessed input interval is one affine activation region, the initial case of the layer induction in proof step 3.1; no width-zero folding block is claimed.

The terminal continuation with no layers left is explicitly R_{L+1}(r)=1. At rank r=0 the recurrence sum has its j=0 term, so it is one-term rather than empty. Proof step 2.1 inducts backward from exactly this terminal base.

The Statement explicitly admits H=0 hidden layers. Then the empty product is one and the affine output is affine on the entire interval, as concluded in proof step 2.1. The formula involving U/H is restricted to H>=1 and is not evaluated at zero.

The multidimensional bound includes L=1. Its product over layers1 through L-1 is then empty and equals one; proof step 3.1 uses the last-layer hyperplane arrangement directly on the unmodified input cube. Each actual layer width and input dimension still meets its positive lower bound.
